items.title: No Surprises Act claim-fight umpires demand quicker answers: NAIRO - BenefitsPRO
items.reason: This item directly addresses the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process—a core implementation mechanism—and reports on NAIRO's demands for operational improvements, which constitutes a substantive development in how the IDR system is functioning.
items.summary: The National Association of Independent Review Organizations (NAIRO) is demanding faster response timelines from the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process, which adjudicates balance-billing disputes between providers and insurers. The article reports on NAIRO's push for quicker answers/turnaround times in IDR determinations, indicating growing operational pressure within the system that processes claim disputes under the federal balance-billing protections. This development affects healthcare providers, insurers, and IDR entities by highlighting implementation challenges in the NSA's dispute-resolution mechanism, which is critical for revenue-cycle teams managing out-of-network claim denials and appeals.

items.title: NYC, EmblemHealth to pay $53M worth of copays back to 250,000 city retirees in new settlement - amNewYork
items.reason: This is a settlement involving a major payer (EmblemHealth) and a regulatory/enforcement action by NYC regarding improper copay collection from retirees, which directly falls under payer litigation and enforcement actions.
items.summary: New York City and EmblemHealth reached a settlement requiring the payer to return $53 million in copays to approximately 250,000 city retirees. The settlement addresses copay overcharges or improper collections from this retiree population. This enforcement action by NYC demonstrates regulatory pressure on payers regarding claims administration and member billing practices, which impacts revenue-cycle teams' understanding of payer compliance requirements and potential exposure to similar enforcement actions across other jurisdictions.
